note: Originals must be written by a real person. Never generate one — the piece collapses if the centrepiece is machine-written. The three versions under each are generated polish, which is the point.

letters.author: Bhuvan
letters.blurb: Written before any of this ran. Pangram reads it 1.0 human.
letters.original:
Amma,

I'm coming home this winter break. I miss you a lot. Sometimes when I come back from work, I feel like eating your food, but then I have to cook something myself. I know I don't talk much when you call me. Most of the time I am busy with something or the other. Sorry Amma. This time when I come home, I just want to sit with you, eat good food and talk about everything that happened here. I even miss you scolding me for sleeping late. I never thought I would miss all these things.

See you soon Amma.

Love,
Bhuvan

versions.text:
Amma,

I'm coming home this winter break. I miss you a lot. Sometimes when I come back from work, I feel like eating your food, but then I have to cook something myself. I know I don't talk much when you call. Most of the time I'm busy with one thing or another. Sorry, Amma. This time when I come home, I just want to sit with you, eat good food, and talk about everything that's happened here. I even miss you scolding me for sleeping late. I never thought I would miss all of these things.

See you soon, Amma.

Love,
Bhuvan

Amma,

I'll be home for winter break, and I can't wait. I miss you more than I know how to say. Some evenings I come back from work wanting your cooking, and end up making something for myself instead. I know I don't say much when you call — most days I'm caught up in one thing or another, and I'm sorry for that. When I'm home I want to sit beside you, eat properly, and tell you everything that's happened here. I even miss being scolded for sleeping in. I never expected to miss these things.

See you soon, Amma.

Love,
Bhuvan

Dear Amma,

I'll be home for the winter, and the thought of it carries me through the week. Distance has a way of clarifying things. I've learned to cook for myself, though nothing I make tastes the way your kitchen does, and I've learned that being busy is a poor excuse for being quiet. Forgive me for the calls I've rushed through. What I want most is simple: to sit beside you, to eat well, to tell you everything. Strange, the things absence makes precious — even the small corrections I once resented.

Until very soon,
Bhuvan
